title: Microglia sculpt circuits
objective: Explain how microglia prune synapses during development and why that matters beyond immunity.

steps.title: Immune cells that shape wiring
steps.body:
Microglia don't just defend; they help **build** circuits. During development, many extra synapses form and the weaker ones are removed. Microglia carry out much of that removal, **[[synaptic pruning]]**, by engulfing synaptic material.

So an immune cell is a sculptor of neural circuits.

steps.title: Borrowing a tagging system
steps.body:
How do microglia know which synapses to remove? One mechanism reuses the immune **[[complement]]** system: complement proteins (like C1q and C3) tag less-active synapses, and microglia engulf the tagged ones (2007, 2012).

It's the opsonization idea from B2-L3, 'tag, then eat,' applied to synapses instead of microbes.

flag.note: Complement-mediated pruning is one important mechanism among several; its role varies by region and stage.

visual.alt: A neuron with two synapses: the weaker one is tagged with complement protein, and a microglial cell extends a process and engulfs it, while the active untagged synapse remains.
visual.caption: Complement tags the weak synapse; the microglion engulfs it.

steps.prompt: Pruning is described as activity-dependent. What does that mean?
options: That all synapses are removed equally, regardless of their activity
That less-active synapses are preferentially tagged and then removed
That only the strongest, most-active synapses get pruned away
That activity plays no role in deciding which synapses survive
steps.explanation: 'Use it or lose it': weaker, less-active synapses are more likely to be tagged and pruned, refining circuits based on activity.

variants.setup: Developmental synaptic pruning is described as 'activity-dependent'.
options: All synapses are removed equally, whatever their activity
Less-active synapses are preferentially tagged and removed
Only the strongest, most-active synapses are removed
Activity plays no role in what survives
variants.reveal: 'Use it or lose it': weaker, less-active synapses are more likely to be tagged and pruned, refining circuits by activity.

steps.prompt: How is complement-mediated pruning like antibody opsonization (B2-L3)?
options: Both work by editing the DNA of the target they act on
Both tag a target so that a phagocyte then engulfs it
Both produce antibodies that circulate and bind their target
They are unrelated processes that only look superficially similar
steps.explanation: Same logic, different target: a molecular tag marks the item (microbe or synapse) and a phagocyte (macrophage or microglion) removes it. Immunology concepts recur in neuroscience.

variants.setup: Complement tags weak synapses; antibodies opsonize microbes.
variants.prompt: How are these two processes alike?
options: Both edit the target's DNA
Both tag a target so a phagocyte engulfs it
Both produce circulating antibodies
They are unrelated and only look similar
variants.reveal: Same logic, different target: a molecular tag marks the item and a phagocyte (microglion or macrophage) removes it.

steps.setup: In a mouse lacking a complement component needed for tagging, what might you expect in developing circuits?
options: More aggressive pruning, stripping away even active synapses
Reduced pruning, so surplus synapses may linger in the circuit
No synapses form at all in the developing circuit
Neurons die immediately once the component is removed
steps.reveal: Lose the tag and the 'eat me' signal weakens, so pruning is reduced and surplus synapses can linger, the loss-of-function test of the pruning model.

flag.note: Phenotypes depend on the specific component, region and developmental stage.

variants.prompt: A mouse lacks the complement component that tags synapses. What do you predict for its developing circuits?
options: More aggressive pruning, stripping away even active synapses
Reduced pruning, so surplus synapses may linger in the circuit
No synapses form at all in the developing circuit
Neurons die immediately once the component is removed
variants.explanation: Lose the 'eat me' tag and pruning weakens, so excess synapses persist — the loss-of-function test of the model.
